record.original_question: Develop a general theory of realizations of k-orbit polytopes by geometrically k-orbit realizations of k-orbit abstract polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of k-orbit polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) satisfy the standard axioms: it has a unique minimum and maximum element, every maximal chain (flag) has length n+1, it is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any two faces F < G with rank(G) - rank(F) = 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G). The automorphism group of an abstract polytope P acts on the set of its flags, partitioning them into orbits; P is called a k-orbit abstract polytope if this action has exactly k orbits.

A geometric realization of an abstract polytope P of rank n is a mapping of its faces into Euclidean space (in a suitable, structure-preserving sense) that assigns to each face a geometric object so that incidence relations are respected. A realization is said to be geometrically k-orbit if its Euclidean symmetry group acts on the flags of the realization with exactly k orbits, matching the combinatorial flag-orbit structure of the underlying abstract polytope.

Problem. Develop a general theory of realizations of k-orbit abstract polytopes by geometrically k-orbit realizations. In particular, provide a framework (analogous to McMullen's realization-cone theory for regular polytopes) that classifies, parametrizes, or otherwise describes all geometrically k-orbit Euclidean realizations of an arbitrary k-orbit abstract polytope, including conditions under which such realizations exist and a description of the moduli of such realizations up to similarity.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is broadly programmatic, calling for a general theory analogous to McMullen's realization theory of regular polytopes but extended to the k-orbit setting. While McMullen's theory for regular (1-orbit) polytopes is well developed and progress has been made on combinatorial aspects of k-orbit polytopes (e.g., characterizing their automorphism groups as coset geometries), no comprehensive theory of geometrically k-orbit realizations of k-orbit abstract polytopes appears in the literature. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes via coset geometries, addressing combinatorial rather than geometric realization aspects.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses combinatorial structure of k-orbit polytopes but not a general geometric realization theory.

status_evidence.title: Realizations of abstract regular polytopes from a representation theoretic view
status_evidence.snippet: Develops realization theory for abstract regular (1-orbit) polytopes via representation theory.
status_evidence.claim: Realization theory is well developed for the 1-orbit case; an extension to general k-orbit polytopes is not established.
